findings.title: deleteCacheMutation does not invalidate connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cacheUpdatedAt in UI
findings.body: After a successful cache deletion, the user's dropdown still shows the old 'Last updated' timestamp because the `deleteCacheMutation` only calls `onSuccess?.()` and shows a toast, but unlike `disconnectMutation` (lines 53-65) it never invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars`. Since `connectedCalendarsHandler` maps `cacheUpdatedAt` from the DB on each query, the displayed status will remain stuck on the pre-deletion value until the user manually reloads. Either invalidate the query (mirroring `disconnectMutation`'s `onSettled`) or refetch the calendars query on success so the cache status reflects reality.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds ignores expiresAt, surfacing expired cache rows
findings.body: `getCachedAvailability` (lines 121-129) explicitly filters on `expiresAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now()) }` so lookups refuse to serve stale entries, but the new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` only groups by `credentialId` with no `expiresAt` filter. Result: once a row's `expiresAt` is in the past, `getCachedAvailability` returns null yet the UI still displays a 'Last updated' timestamp from that expired row, giving the user the misleading impression that their cache is fresh. Add the same `expiresAt: { gte: new Date(Date.now()) }` (or filter out expired entries in the `Map` mapping) so the UI status matches the lookup behavior.

findings.title: updateManyByCredentialId called with empty data {} may be a no-op
findings.body: `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is invoked with an empty update payload under the comment 'Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for all calendars under this credential'. Depending on Prisma's behavior with `data: {}` (some Prisma versions reject it or skip generating the SET clause, in which case the auto-managed `@updatedAt` is not refreshed), this can silently do nothing. Either set the field explicitly (`updatedAt: new Date()`) or remove the call if updating `updatedAt` is intentionally handled elsewhere (the PR notes themselves flag this as a candidate for removal since the UI uses `CalendarCache.cacheUpdatedAt` instead).

findings.title: Migration warnings comment contradicts the SQL default
findings.body: The header comment generated by Prisma reads 'Added the required column `updatedAt` to the `CalendarCache` table without a default value. This is not possible if the table is not empty.' but the SQL right below uses `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()`. The comments are misleading and will confuse anyone reviewing the migration history; update the warning so it matches the actual change ('with default `NOW()` for legacy rows').

findings.title: BSD-only sed syntax makes script fail on Linux
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD sed (macOS) syntax where the empty argument after `-i` disables backup file creation. On GNU sed (Linux/Ubuntu/etc. CI runners and most dev containers) this is interpreted as a backup suffix and produces an error or an unexpected backup file. Either detect the platform and dispatch to `sed -i.bak` followed by `rm`, or use a portable idiom such as `sed -i.bak -E "..." "$ENV_FILE" && rm "$ENV_FILE.bak"`.

findings.title: No tests for deleteCacheHandler, getCacheStatusByCredentialIds, or CredentialActionsDropdown
findings.body: Three new pieces of behavior ship with the PR (deleteCache tRPC handler with ownership check, getCacheStatusByCredentialIds repository method, and the deleteCachedData flow in CredentialActionsDropdown), but no unit/integration tests are added. The PR review checklist itself called this out as a known limitation. At minimum, add a handler test that covers the cross-user denial path (requesting a credential belonging to another user) and the success path, plus a UI test for the dropdown rendering and invalidation behavior.
